quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #17
										  					
  

37 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: You are driving on a highway with two solid yellow lines dividing it. You may:

options.text: Cross these lines only to turn left into or out of an alley, private road, or driveway.
Cross these lines to pass other vehicles if there is no oncoming traffic.
Never cross these lines.
Cross these lines only to make a U-turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cross these lines only to turn left into or out of an alley, private road, or driveway.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean no passing is allowed in either direction. You can only cross them to turn left into or out of an alley, private road, or driveway.

questions.question: You had an upsetting incident at work and feel angry. When you reach your car, you should:

options.text: Play loud music so you won't think about it.
Drive fast on the highway to release your anger.
Wait a few minutes to calm down before you drive.
Stop at a bar for drinks before driving home.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait a few minutes to calm down before you drive.
questions.explanation: If you are upset or angry, take time to calm down before driving. Driving while emotional is dangerous for you and others on the road.

questions.question: When you meet an aggressive driver, you should:

options.text: Do not make eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
Cut them off to slow them down.
Follow closely behind them to retaliate.
Show them you disapprove of their driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not make eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Stay calm and increase the distance between your car and theirs. Slow down and let them pass. Do not look at them or make gestures.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, you should:

options.text: Call the police right away.
Stay calm and move away from the aggressive driver.
Flash your lights to show the driver they are wrong.
Do something aggressive back to get even.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay calm and move away from the aggressive driver.
questions.explanation: Stay calm and move out of their way. Trying to get revenge makes the situation more dangerous.

questions.question: A red and white triangular sign means:

options.text: Slow down if an emergency vehicle is near.
Look both ways before crossing.
Always stop completely at the intersection.
Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: This is a yield sign. Slow down as you approach the intersection and let other vehicles and pedestrians go first. Be ready to stop if necessary.

questions.question: To pass a slower vehicle on a two-lane road with traffic in both directions, you must:

options.text: Not cross the center line.
Flash your lights at oncoming cars.
Use the shoulder.
Use the lane for oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the lane for oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: Passing on a two-lane road means using the lane meant for oncoming traffic. Only do this if it is safe and legal.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Do not drink if you will drive.
The road is slippery when wet.
The road curves ahead.
A hill is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road is slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road becomes slippery when wet.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: A divided highway is starting.
A steep hill is ahead.
The overhead bridge has limited clearance.
Two lanes of traffic are about to merge.

questions.correctAnswerText: The overhead bridge has limited clearance.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the bridge ahead has a limited height. Do not pass if your vehicle is taller than the height shown on the sign.

questions.question: You may cross a dashed white line:

options.text: At any time.
Only during the day.
When it is safe to change lanes.
Only when passing a motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it is safe to change lanes.
questions.explanation: Dashed white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction. You may cross them to change lanes or pass if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: A green arrow on a lane control signal means:

options.text: You may use this lane.
No vehicles are allowed in this lane.
You have the right-of-way.
You must move into this lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may use this lane.
questions.explanation: A steady green arrow pointing down means you may use that lane.

questions.question: You are waiting in the intersection to turn left. What should you do?

options.text: Signal and turn your wheels to the left.
Signal and keep your wheels straight.
Flash your headlights to ask drivers to let you through.
Drive around a car that blocks you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal and keep your wheels straight.
questions.explanation: Always signal before turning or changing lanes. Keep your wheels straight while waiting to turn left. If a car hits you from behind, straight wheels keep you from being pushed into oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What does a single dashed white line between lanes mean?

options.text: Drivers may pass, even if it is dangerous.
Lanes move in opposite directions.
Drivers may not pass.
Drivers may pass if it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers may pass if it is safe.
questions.explanation: White lines separate lanes moving in the same direction. Dashed white lines can be crossed to pass or change lanes if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: The traffic light turns yellow as you near an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to pass through before the red light.
Brake hard to stop right away.
Be ready to stop in the middle of the intersection.
Be ready to stop before you reach the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop before you reach the intersection.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means the light will turn red soon. Be ready to stop before the intersection if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: How can drivers prevent accidents on long trips?

options.text: Stop every couple of hours to rest.
Avoid medicine that causes drowsiness.
Drive no more than 300-400 miles per day.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Stop every couple of hours to stretch and rest. Drive no more than 300-400 miles per day. Get good sleep before your trip. Do not take medicine that makes you drowsy.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should NOT:

options.text: Check your side and rearview mirrors.
Use your turn signal.
Check for other drivers moving into your lane.
Use your cell phone to call police to check if the road is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your cell phone to call police to check if the road is clear.
questions.explanation: Check your side and rearview mirrors for traffic behind you. Use your turn signal to tell other drivers you plan to change lanes. Look for other drivers also moving into your lane.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: All traffic must turn.
Turn right at the intersection.
Parking area ahead.
A crossroad is ahead. Watch for traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: A crossroad is ahead. Watch for traffic.
questions.explanation: This sign warns drivers that a crossroad is coming.

questions.question: When turning, you must ____ your speed.

options.text: Increase
Keep the same
Change
Decrease

questions.correctAnswerText: Decrease
questions.explanation: Slow down when turning. This helps you control your vehicle, stay in your lane, and react to unexpected situations.

questions.question: When another car is tailgating you:

options.text: Move to the right lane if one is open.
If no right lane exists, wait until the road ahead is clear and slow down gradually so the tailgater will pass.
Never brake suddenly.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Move to the right lane if available. If not, wait until the road is clear and slow down gradually to let the tailgater pass. Never brake suddenly, as this increases the chance of being hit from behind.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Watch for bicycles.
Bicycles are not allowed.
Bicycle repair shop ahead.
Bicycles have the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for bicycles.
questions.explanation: This sign warns drivers that bicycles may be in the area.

questions.question: What is the purpose of highway markings?

options.text: They are usually not important.
They are only found in construction zones.
They give information to drivers.
They are usually red and blue.

questions.correctAnswerText: They give information to drivers.
questions.explanation: Highway markings give information to drivers. They help position vehicles on roads, show safe passing zones, and warn drivers about upcoming conditions.

questions.question: What are regulatory signs?

options.text: They are placed everywhere there is danger.
They tell drivers what they must or must not do.
They are diamond-shaped and yellow or green.
They warn drivers about school zones.

questions.correctAnswerText: They tell drivers what they must or must not do.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are usually rectangular with black markings on white. They tell drivers what they must or must not do. They may show speed limits, no passing rules, or other driving rules.

questions.question: This sign warns you that you are approaching:

options.text: An intersection.
A crosswalk.
A railroad crossing.
A blasting zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: A railroad crossing.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a railroad crossing is ahead.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: The left lane is for vehicles with a certain number of people inside.
Certain turns are allowed from certain lanes.
Do not enter.
Both lanes must merge smoothly.

questions.correctAnswerText: The left lane is for vehicles with a certain number of people inside.
questions.explanation: This is a high occupancy vehicle (HOV) lane. It is for buses and cars with the driver plus one or more passengers, as shown on the sign.

questions.question: You cannot park within ____ of a fire hydrant.

options.text: 10 feet
15 feet
30 feet
45 feet

questions.correctAnswerText: 15 feet
questions.explanation: Do not park within 15 feet of a fire hydrant. Park only where it is legal and where other drivers can see your car.

questions.question: Another driver is trying to pass you. What should you do?

options.text: Pull off the road.
Signal when it is safe for them to pass.
Check for oncoming traffic and slow down to let them pass safely.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for oncoming traffic and slow down to let them pass safely.
questions.explanation: Stay in the right lane when another driver passes on the left. Check for oncoming traffic and adjust your speed so the passing car can move back into the right lane easily.

questions.question: You are in the right lane of a highway and want to move to the left lane. What should you do?

options.text: Look in your rearview mirror for traffic behind you.
Look over your left shoulder for traffic in your blind spot.
Look in your side mirror and turn on your signal.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move. Always signal before changing lanes.

questions.question: Which statement about railroad crossings is true?

options.text: It is illegal to go around lowered gates.
You must stop when a flagger tells you to stop.
Not all railroad crossings have flashing red lights or gates.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger, stop sign, or warning devices like gates or flashing lights tell you to. Not all crossings have these devices. It is illegal to drive around lowered railroad crossing gates.

questions.question: If two drivers reach an open intersection at the same time:

options.text: The driver on the right has the right-of-way.
The driver on the left has the right-of-way.
One driver may continue without stopping.
One driver should honk to give up the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver on the right has the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: If you reach an open intersection at the same time as a vehicle to your right, yield to that vehicle. You may go when it is safe.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Keep right.
Low shoulder.
No parking at any time.
Lane ends.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep right.
questions.explanation: This regulatory sign tells drivers what they must do. It means drivers should keep right to avoid a hazard ahead.

questions.question: What does a single dashed yellow line between traffic mean?

options.text: Drivers may pass if it is safe.
Both lanes go in the same direction.
Drivers may not pass.
Drivers may pass even if it is dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers may pass if it is safe.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic going in opposite directions. A single dashed yellow line means vehicles in both directions can pass. Only pass if you will not interfere with oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What should you do if your accelerator sticks while driving?

options.text: Reach down and try to pull it up.
Shift to park.
Shift to neutral and press the brake steadily.
Turn off the engine.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to neutral and press the brake steadily.
questions.explanation: If your accelerator sticks, keep your eyes on the road. Shift into neutral and press the brake pedal with steady pressure. When safe, pull off the road and turn off the engine.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: One-way road.
No right turn.
Exit.
Sharp right turn ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sharp right turn ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a sharp right turn is ahead.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Hunting area.
State park.
Deer crossing.
Wildlife preserve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Deer crossing.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that deer cross the road in this area. Slow down, watch carefully, and be ready to stop.

questions.question: What color are signs for public recreation areas?

options.text: Orange.
Red.
Green.
Brown.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brown.
questions.explanation: Brown signs show cultural, historical, or public recreation areas. They help you find resources when traveling in unfamiliar places.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: You must drive at this speed.
The highest legal speed on this road is 55 mph.
You must drive through the intersection at this speed.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: The highest legal speed on this road is 55 mph.
questions.explanation: This is a speed limit sign. It shows the maximum legal speed for the road. In rain, snow, ice, or poor conditions, you may need to drive slower than the posted limit.

questions.question: When driving on slick roads, what should you do?

options.text: Make turns more slowly than usual.
Change lanes quickly.
Speed up quickly.
Brake hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make turns more slowly than usual.
questions.explanation: Driving too fast on slippery roads is always dangerous, especially in turns and curves. Approach turns much more slowly than you would on dry roads.

questions.question: What does a green arrow traffic signal mean?

options.text: It is only used on one-way streets.
You can go, but you must turn in the direction the arrow points.
You may go only if the arrow is with a circular green light.
It points the way to an airport.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can go, but you must turn in the direction the arrow points.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you can proceed, but you must turn in the direction shown by the arrow.
